title: Choose the homepage structure
question: The Rye Island world is pinned by your brief, so this round is composition only. The roll dealt three structures for the Weedmaps homepage. Lock one.

options.label: The Territory
options.lineage: the product is literally named for a map
options.thesis: The page opens as the map itself; every listing docks to a place.
options.viewport: A full-bleed area map in linen and ink, open shops pinned in orange, closed in grey. A floating pill bar holds location and the Pickup/Delivery fork. A horizontal rail of storefront cards docks to the bottom edge and scrubs in sync with the map.
options.risk: Maps are heavy on cellular and hostile to a visitor who does not yet know what they want to buy.

options.label: The Counter
options.thesis: The page asks the three questions a good budtender asks, then assembles the shortlist.
options.viewport: One sentence set large in Manrope across the first viewport, with effect, format and budget as inline dropdowns inside the line. As each is answered the sentence completes and a ranked shortlist of products and the shops carrying them assembles underneath.
options.risk: An interstitial between the visitor and the inventory; a returning buyer who already knows what they want will resent being asked.

options.label: The Shelf
options.thesis: You shop the product, not the shop. The retailer is the answer, not the question.
options.viewport: A compact location and mode bar, then the page becomes shelves: flower, pre-rolls, vape, edibles, each a horizontal rail of real products on linen with mono price tickets and the nearest shop that carries it named under each. Deals cut in as an orange-drenched band between shelves.
options.risk: Buries the storefront identity retailers pay for, and needs dense product data before it looks alive.
